newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-TOSHACK LEAVES DEPORTIVO PROBLEMS BEHIND HIM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TOSHACK LEAVES DEPORTIVO PROBLEMS BEHIND HIM.

text.p: John Toshack ended the most trying period of his long managerial career on Sunday when he quit Deportivo Coruna.

Former Wales international striker Toshack, who has had years of managerial experience in Spain, had been long under fire from Deportivo fans and was barracked during Sunday's 2-2 draw with Celta Vigo.
Deportivo club presdident Augusto Lenoiro said Toshack presented his resignation last week but that he had accepted it only after the Celta match.
Toshack will be replaced on a temporary basis by second team coach Jose Manuel Corral. But Deportivo are likely to sign former Valencia coach Luis Aragones for next season.

Despite signing a host of internationals, Deportivo have been struggling to keep in touch with Real Madrid and Barcelona. Problems on the pitch were aggravated when Toshack clashed with club authorities, players and fans.
Toshack joined Deportivo in the close season of 1995 after spells at Real Sociedad and Real Madrid, where he won the 1989-90 Spanish championship with a record goal haul.
But his move to La Coruna seemed doomed to failure from the start.
Veteran manager Arsenio Iglesias had taken Deportivo from the brink of the second division and turned them into serious title contenders.
But Toshack quickly clashed with the star of Iglesias's team -- World Cup striker Bebeto -- and earned the wrath of Deportivo fans by dropping the Brazilian on several occasions.
Deportivo slumped to eighth in the league and failed to gain a place in European competition for the first time since 1992.

Bebeto went back home last summer but Deportivo continued buying Brazilians to play alongside Donato and Mauro Silva and controversial president Lendoiro took advantage of the Bosman ruling on European Union workers' rights by signing a legion of continental players.

Despite the spending spree, Toshack made well-publicised criticism of Lendoiro's strategy and complained that his own ideas were not being taken into account. He also went on record as saying that Deportivo should invest money in training facilities before buying players.
Deportivo started the season with some good results, although commentators were quick to hit out at the negative tactics of their coach.
"(He) turned gold into lead," said one journalist, in reference to the high quality of the Deportivo squad.
Things started to go badly wrong when Barcelona snatched a late winner in the first game of 1997.
Since then it has all gone downhill for Toshack, who told Galician television in January that he was not likely to continue at Deportivo after his contract expired at the end of the season.
Angry fans sprayed grafitti criticising the coach on the walls of the Riazor stadium. One of them, in English, read "Toshack go home".

Problems came to a head in the home game against Athletic Bilbao two weeks ago. Toshack was abused by the crowd for substituting Brazilian midfielder Rivaldo and responded by shouting obscenities at the stands.

To make matters worse Rivaldo joined a long list of players who have brushed with the Welshman. Dressing-room unrest was exacerbated by the strength of a squad which meant many players had only limited chances of playing.

Brazilian midfielder Flavio Conceicao, who was pursued by both Real Madrid and Barcelona before signing for Deportivo in December, failed to turn up for a Cup match after being left out of the starting line-up.
Toshack leaves Deportivo now 15 points adrift of leaders Real and with their Cup hopes over.

There was no word on Sunday as to the immediate future of Toshack, who once formed a famed Liverpool striking partnership with Kevin Keegan, who himself resigned as manager of English premier league Newcastle last month.
